items.t: DSV shares surge on third-quarter revenue beat, share buyback launch
sum: Investing.com -- DSV shares jumped nearly 8% in early Copenhagen trading Wednesday after the company reported better-than-expected third-quarter revenue and announced a 1.5 billion crown share buyback program, first since its acquisition of Schenker.
Third-quarter revenue came in at 80.7 billion Danish crowns, beating analyst estimates of 74.7 billion crowns and marking a 12% increase from a year earlier.
Adjusted net income rose to 4.07 billion crowns, surpassing the consensus estimate of 3.85 billion. However, adjusted EBIT of 6.61 billion crowns came in slightly below the estimate of 6.66 billion.

The Denmark-based transport and logistics firm narrowed its fiscal 2026 adjusted EBIT guidance to 24 billion to 25 billion crowns from a previous range of 23.5 billion to 25.5 billion. The midpoint of 24.5 billion sits above the analyst consensus of 24.41 billion. The company also reduced its expected special items for integration costs to 5.5 billion crowns from 6.5 billion.

Earnings growth was driven by strong results in the Air & Sea and Contract Logistics divisions, supported by cost synergies from the Schenker integration. The Road division saw earnings decline due to negative volume growth and lower productivity stemming from operational issues related to the Schenker integration. Property disposals also contributed to EBIT across all divisions.

The company noted that its demand outlook continues to be affected by rising energy prices and global inflation. DSV expects an effective tax rate of about 28% for 2026, citing the ongoing Schenker integration.

items.t: Aegon completes exchange of all Common Shares B for common stock
sum: 15.10.2026 12:45:00 CEST | GlobeNewswire by notified | Press release

Schiphol, October 15, 2026 - Aegon today announces that it has repurchased all outstanding Common Shares B held by its largest shareholder, Vereniging Aegon Americas, in exchange for common shares with equal voting rights on a 40-to-1 basis, upon completion of which the interim bye-laws approved at Aegon’s Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM) of October 8, 2026, became effective as of today.

Aegon is an international financial services holding company. Aegon’s ambition is to become a leading US life insurance, annuity, and retirement group with international insurance and asset management subsidiaries. Aegon’s portfolio of businesses includes fully-owned businesses in the United States and a global asset manager. On April 15, 2026, Aegon announced an agreement to sell its insurance platform in the UK, Aegon UK, and expects to complete the transaction around the end of 2026. Via insurance joint-ventures in Spain & Portugal, China, and Brazil, and via asset management partnerships in France and China, Aegon creates value by combining Aegon’s international expertise with strong local partners. In addition, Aegon owns a Bermuda-based life insurer and generates value via a strategic shareholding in a market leading Dutch insurance and pensions company.

Aegon’s purpose of helping people live their best lives runs through all its activities. As a leading global investor and employer, Aegon seeks to have a positive impact by addressing critical environmental and societal issues. Aegon is headquartered in Schiphol, the Netherlands, domiciled in Bermuda, and listed on Euronext Amsterdam and the New York Stock Exchange. More information can be found on aegon.com.

items.t: DSV (CPSE:DSV) Climbed, So What Is Behind The Latest Attention?
sum: DSV (CPSE:DSV) has agreed a logistics partnership with Skyways that brings autonomous aircraft into offshore energy supply routes, starting with North Sea operations from Norden, Germany, this fall.

For investors tracking DSV, the new Skyways deal lands after a mixed stretch in the market. The share price has climbed 3.41% over the last day but is down 9.27% over 30 days and 27.16% over 90 days, while the 1 year total shareholder return has declined 8.90%. This signals pressure on longer term sentiment even as short term momentum shows signs of stabilising around the recent DKK1,199 level. Operational developments such as the Porsche Carrera Cup logistics work and this autonomous aircraft move are reshaping how the business is being priced for risk and future demand.
Scan other logistics and infrastructure plays that could benefit from similar shifts toward automation by reviewing our curated list of 90 AI infrastructure stocks alongside DSV.
DSV now finds itself with a fresh automation story, a softer one year return and a DKK1,199 share price. Does that mix still leave more upside for new buyers than downside if things disappoint?

On the most followed view, DSV is priced at a clear markdown. The narrative fair value of DKK2,194 sits well above the recent DKK1,199 close, which puts fresh weight on how long term holders frame the risk and reward trade off.

DSV just pulled off the biggest deal in its history: the Schenker acquisition, instantly making it the world's #1 freight forwarder. That is not just a headline, it is a game-changer for pricing power, scale, and cross-selling.

According to Bejgal, that fair value estimate is built using a 6.36% discount rate and a DKK2,190 target that assumes revenue growth of 7.91% a year, earnings reaching DKK23b by 2029 and an exit P/E of 28x. Those inputs paint a picture where the recent share price implies a large gap to what this narrative expects DSV could generate if those forecasts hold.

sum: At the close on September 16, 2026, DSV stock finished at DKK 1,255 on Nasdaq Copenhagen, down 2.2 percent from the prior session. The shares touched a fresh 52-week low around that level as the stock extended its recent weakness.

DSV A/S (ISIN DK0060079531) saw its share price move between an intraday low near DKK 1,255 and a day high slightly above that mark on Nasdaq Copenhagen on September 16, 2026, before closing at DKK 1,255. Per exchange data, the drop of 2.2 percent came after the stock had already been trending lower over recent sessions, bringing it to the bottom of its 52-week range. As Investing.com reported on September 15, 2026, the shares touched a fresh 52-week low around DKK 1,255 while analysts highlighted that they remain broadly positive on the company, which helped frame the session as pressure driven more by valuation and market sentiment than a specific new corporate setback. According to data from Nasdaq Copenhagen, DSV’s move contrasted with a more stable performance in the broader Danish equity market on the same day, underscoring that the stock underperformed its home index as it slipped to that new low.

Today, investors are watching whether DSV can stabilize after the latest 52-week low, especially as recent analyst commentary has remained supportive. As The Globe and Mail noted, Barclays recently reiterated a buy stance on DSV shares, while Goldman Sachs maintained a hold rating, keeping broker attention on the name. This mix of cautious market pricing and generally constructive analyst views may shape trading in DSV today as the stock heads into the open near its 52-week low. Broader European transport and logistics sentiment, as well as moves in key equity indices, are also likely to influence DSV’s session, given the company’s sensitivity to global trade and economic expectations.

items.t: DSV loves RFD: Logistics provider and airport hook up over air cargo
sum: Global logistics giant DSV on Saturday launched a weekly dedicated air charter service from Seoul, South Korea, to Chicago-Rockford International Airport through the end of August, underscoring the airport’s growing popularity as a cargo relief valve for crowded O’Hare airport, an hour’s drive to the east.
DSV has contracted with all-cargo airline Atlas Air to operate a Boeing 747 jumbo jet to Chicago-Rockford, continuing on to Huntsville, Alabama, and then Luxembourg, the route.

On Tuesdays, a DSV-controlled Boeing 777 from Shanghai, China, will land at Chicago-Rockford (RFD) before traveling to Incheon airport in Seoul. And on Fridays a 777 will depart Incheon and return, before heading to Jinan, China. In total, DSV is providing eight flight operations per week through RFD, primarily to support healthcare customers, said Mohamed Siraj, DSV’s vice president Air Direct / Global Gateways via email.

DSV, the third-largest logistics service provider in the world based on revenue, began utilizing RFD in November when it began weekly charter flights from Shanghai. In June, an inbound service from Luxembourg began. All the flights are operated by Atlas Air and flow through RFD on their way to other destinations in the DSV network.

“Incheon is one of Asia’s most important cargo hubs, and with this new service, DSV can provide reliable capacity and connectivity via the network we are building through Rockford,” Siraj said in a joint news release last week. “The airport has consistently demonstrated the operational reliability and flexibility needed to support scheduled international freighter services, making it a natural choice as we continue developing our air cargo operations.”

And DSV isn’t finished adding air freight service to Chicago-Rockford. The company plans to introduce a scheduled service connecting RFD to Chennai, India, later this year because of high demand from the tech sector.
The lease arrangement with Atlas Air is flexible, allowing DSV to adjust capacity and deploy aircraft where customer demand is greatest in its network.
